questions.question: Evaluate the importance of social interaction in a child’s motor skill development during team sports. How does this compare to individual practice? / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Evaluate the importance of social interaction in a child's motor skill development during team
  • sports. How does this compare to individual practice? [E]/[C05]
  • Ans. Social interaction in team sports is crucial because it necessitates the use of complex,
  • coordinated motor skills like passing and defensive positioning that depend on reading teammates.
  • It provides a dynamic, unpredictable environment that fosters applied motor learning and
  • decision-making under pressure. Individual practice typically focuses on refining isolated
  • fundamental skills (e.g., shooting technique) in a predictable setting. Therefore, while individual
  • practice builds the foundation, social interaction during team play is essential for translating basic
  • skills into functional, game-ready competence.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain why an athlete suffering from depression might also experience a decline in their athletic performance / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain why an athlete suffering from depression might also experience a decline in their
  • athletic performance [E]/[COS]
  • Ans. Depression fundamentally impairs concentration, energy levels, and motivation , making it
  • difficult for the athlete to maintain the rigorous training regimen and mental focus required for
  • high-level competition. This diminished psychological state directly translates to a decline in
  • physical effort, impaired decision-making under pressure, and reduced adherence to the necessary
  • skill-maintenance routines.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: How does overthinking or anxiety disrupt focus during a game? / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• How does overthinking or anxiety disrupt focus during a game? [U]/[C05]
  • Ans. Cognitive Overload: Overthinking shifts the athlete's attention internally, causing a mental
  • struggle between repetitive negative thoughts (like fear of failure or self-doubt).
  • Impaired Attentional Control: Anxiety impairs the brain's ability to selectively focus on relevant
  • environmental cues (e.g., the position of the opponent, the trajectory of the ball) and increases focus
  • on irrelevant, distracting stimuli, leading to slower reaction times and poor, non-instinctive
  • decision-making (known as "choking").

questions.question: Discuss the role of goal-setting in enhancing motivation among athletes. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the role of goal-setting in enhancing motivation among athletes [E]/[CO4]
  • Ans. Goal-setting is a fundamental psychological tool that significantly enhances athlete motivation
  • by providing direction, clarity, and feedback.
  • These are the five key roles goal-setting plays in boosting athlete motivation:
  • • Directs Attention and Effort: Goals clarify exactly what the athlete needs to focus on
  • (e.g., improving free throw percentage rather than just "getting better").
  • • Mobilizes Effort and Persistence: Setting challenging yet realistic goals encourages
  • athletes to put forth more effort and for a longer duration.
  • • Provides a Benchmark for Feedback: Goals allow athletes to objectively measure their
  • progress, which is a major source of motivation.
  • • Fosters Task Cohesion (Shared Goals): In team sports, establishing shared team goals
  • (e.g., win the championship, reduce turnovers) creates a collective identity and purpose.
  • • Reduces Anxiety and Enhances Self-Efficacy: Focusing on process goals (e.g., execute a
  • specific defensive technique) rather than solely on outcome goals (e.g., win the game) gives
  • athletes a sense of control over their performance.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: As a sports coach, create a simple, two-part proactive plan to help your athletes build resilience and prevent performance anxiety from developing into an abnormal behavior / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• As a sports coach, create a simple, two-part proactive plan to help your athletes build resilience
  • and prevent performance anxiety from developing into an abnormal behaviour
  • [E]/[CO5)
  • Ans. Two-part proactive plan for a sports coach to build athlete resilience and prevent performance
  • anxiety:
  • Part 1: Proactive Resilience Training (Focus on Process)
  • Establish a culture that prioritizes process goals over purely outcome goals. Consistently praise and
  • reinforce effort, learning from mistakes, and adherence to strategy, rather than just wins or scores.
  • This shift teaches athletes that their value is not dependent solely on results, which directly builds
  • self-worth and self-efficacy.
  • Part 2: Cognitive & Emotional Skill-Building (Focus on Control)
  • Teach simple, non-negotiable pre-performance routines (PPRs) that focus attention on the task at
  • hand, not the outcome. A PPR might include three deep breaths, a positive self-talk cue and a
  • specific physical action.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Define the relationship between sports psychology and the field of physiology. / [CO1] [15x2 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Define the relationship between sports psychology and the field of physiology [K]/[CO1]
  • Ans. The relationship between sports psychology and the field of physiology is synergistic and bi-
  • directional,
  • The mind affects the body and the body affects the mind. They represent the two essential
  • components of athletic performance, often studied together under the umbrella of Kinesiology.
  • • Mind-Body Connection (Psychophysiology): Sports psychology investigates how mental
  • states (e.g., anxiety, focus, motivation) cause physiological changes.
  • • Performance Optimization: Physiology (Exercise Physiology) measures physical capacity
  • while sports psychology develops mental skills (e.g., imagery, self-talk) to ensure an athlete
  • can maximally utilize that physical capacity under pressure.
  • • Training and Adaptation: Psychological factors are necessary for athletes to consistently
  • engage in the demanding training required to achieve physiological adaptation (e.g.,
  • muscle hypertrophy or increased endurance).
  • • Rehabilitation: Sports psychology assists athletes with the (e.g., managing pain,
  • maintaining optimism), directly supporting the physiological healing and re-training
  • prescribed by physiologists and physical therapists.
  • [15x2=30]
